question: What is the primary goal of pharmacological treatment for peptic ulcer disease?

options.C: Promote ulcer healing and relieve pain
options.D: Thicken the outer muscle layer of the stomach

explanation: Medical management aims to heal mucosal sores and manage patient discomfort while addressing underlying aggressive factors. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h1)

question: Peptic ulcers develop when aggressive factors like gastric acid overwhelm which body mechanism?
explanation: Ulceration occurs when destructive elements overpower the protective lining of the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which enzyme system is directly inhibited by proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)?
explanation: PPIs target the hydrogen-potassium pump on parietal cells to block acid release into the stomach lumen. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h2)

question: When is the best time for a patient to take their daily proton pump inhibitor dose?

options.A: Thirty minutes before the first meal
options.B: Right after a heavy afternoon meal
options.C: Immediately before going to sleep at night

explanation: Taking the medication before breakfast ensures maximum drug availability when proton pumps are activated by food intake. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of H2-receptor antagonists?

options.A: Competitively block histamine receptors on parietal cells
options.B: Eradicate Helicobacter pylori bacteria from the gut
options.C: Neutralize existing acid in the stomach lumen
options.D: Form a physical barrier over the ulcer crater

explanation: H2RAs prevent histamine from stimulating parietal cells, thereby reducing the volume and acidity of gastric secretions. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which patient group requires extra caution and monitoring when receiving H2-receptor antagonists due to potential confusion?

options.A: Young adults with acute muscle strain
options.D: Pregnant women in the first trimester

explanation: Decreased kidney function can lead to drug accumulation, increasing the risk of central nervous system toxicity like confusion. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of antacids in the stomach?

options.A: Irreversible inhibition of the proton pump
options.C: Chemical neutralization of existing hydrochloric acid
options.D: Suppression of histamine release from mast cells

explanation: Antacids act locally to buffer gastric acid and increase pH without stopping ongoing acid production. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient taking a magnesium-based antacid as part of ulcer management is most likely to experience which side effect?
explanation: Magnesium salts draw water into the intestinal lumen through an osmotic effect, commonly resulting in loose stools. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h4)

question: How does sucralfate primarily protect the gastric mucosa?

options.A: Permanently neutralizes all hydrochloric acid in the gut
options.B: Destroys the cell walls of Helicobacter pylori
options.C: Stimulates immediate closure of the pyloric sphincter
options.D: Forms a sticky protective gel over ulcer craters

explanation: In an acidic environment, sucralfate polymerizes into a paste-like substance that adheres directly to ulcer sites. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is misoprostol frequently prescribed for patients taking long-term nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs?

options.A: It speeds up the systemic elimination of the NSAID
options.B: It prevents the bacterial overgrowth caused by NSAIDs
options.C: It masks joint pain so the NSAID dose can be lowered
options.D: It replaces protective prostaglandins depleted by NSAIDs

explanation: NSAIDs block prostaglandin synthesis, reducing mucosal defense; misoprostol supplies synthetic prostaglandins to restore this protection. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary causative organism linked to most peptic ulcers requiring antibiotic therapy?
explanation: This spiral bacterium colonizes the gastric mucosa, weakening the protective lining and causing chronic inflammation. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why are multiple antibiotics used simultaneously when treating a Helicobacter pylori infection?

options.A: To speed up the healing of the liver and kidneys
options.B: To completely neutralize all stomach acid production
options.C: To eliminate the need for any dietary restrictions
options.D: To prevent the development of antimicrobial resistance

explanation: Combination therapy ensures the bacteria are fully eradicated and lowers the chance of treatment failure due to resistant strains. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h6)

question: A patient taking a multi-drug regimen for Helicobacter pylori asks why they must finish all pills even after pain stops. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Unfinished pills will spoil if kept in the kitchen cabinet
options.B: Stopping early can cause the infection to return and become drug-resistant
options.C: The doctor requires empty bottles to confirm you followed instructions
options.D: The remaining pills are only vitamins to help your energy levels

explanation: Incomplete antibiotic courses fail to clear the bacteria completely and promote the survival of resistant strains. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which symptom reported by a peptic ulcer patient requires immediate medical reporting?
explanation: Melena indicates gastrointestinal bleeding, which is a serious complication of peptic ulcer disease needing prompt evaluation. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h7)
